findings.what: The rule 'The average becomes 207 × cos α' arrives with only 'The part below the line subtracts' before it, so the step that makes it is missing: the slice from α to 180° + α has area cos α − cos(180° + α) = 2 cos α, against a whole hump's 2. The brief asks for every phase-control average to be derived on screen, and screen 11 depends on this rule.

findings.where: Screens 10 and 11, the power factor readout and screen 11's Why

Screen 11's Why then uses '0.9 × 0.5' as given, so add one sentence that a block is not a sine and scores 2√2 ÷ π, about 0.9, even in step.

The text is 88 words, and the finished caption under the picture adds 21 more ('Fired at 30°, the current block starts 30° after the voltage. The output averages 179 V, at a power factor of 0.78.'), which repeat both readouts, so the screen carries about 109 words against the 90-word limit; split the power-factor half onto its own SHOW screen or cut the caption.

findings.where: Screen 9 'A fan on a dimmer' Why, against screen 12 'The soft starter'
findings.what: Screen 9's Why says a motor's coil keeps its current flowing past the zero but never says what that does to a lamp dimmer. Three screens later, back-to-back thyristors phase-control a motor with no word on why that is fine, so Dan meets what looks like a contradiction. One sentence closes it: a soft starter or fan controller is built for a coil's late current, and a lamp dimmer is not.

findings.where: Screen 2 'A diode with a gate', its read sentence
findings.what: The read-through uses the read in place of the text, and this read ('With the cursor at 360°, the heater's voltage is shaded from 90° to 180° only...') names a cursor that the still does not draw (cursorOn is false at 360°). It also drops what a thyristor is, that it latches, and that a pulse at 135° changes nothing, so the Book's first SHOW page never defines the device.

'Past 90° it would turn negative. Power would then flow from the DC side back to the supply' sits under a battery charger, but a battery wired to be charged cannot drive current that way; its current would simply die. Inversion needs a DC source that pushes against the bridge, such as a DC motor being driven, so say that, or say the battery would have to be the other way round.

Explain and Practice carry nine footnotes, and most sit on plain statements he would never look up: the triac's back-to-back thyristors, firing again every cycle, the power factor falling, and thyristor chargers for NiCd. The rule allows a few, on rules or values only, so keep the hydrogen limits and perhaps the holding current, and drop the rest.

findings.where: Screen 2 'A diode with a gate', 'Pulse the gate again at 135°'
findings.what: The words never say to move the Time slider to 135° first. Pressed straight after Play, the button sees the cursor at 360° and says 'the supply is at zero', which misses the point, so write 'Set the time to 135°, then pulse the gate. Nothing changes.'

Each read replaces its screen's words in the read-through and keeps only what the picture shows, so the Book never defines the firing angle, a controlled rectifier, the triac or the choke, or says why the power factor falls. Keep each screen's defining sentence in its read and drop only the 'Drag' lines.

'Each half keeps exactly half its area of squares' is an awkward phrase, and its reason is skipped. The squared hump is symmetrical about 90° too, just as screen 4's hump was, so say 'the squared wave is symmetrical too, so firing at 90° keeps half its heating'.

The finish line says a thyristor's gate is 'never' when it stops and drops the 'ordinary' that Explain uses. The brief names the GTO thyristor 'named, not taught', but this lesson never names it, so 'ordinary' points at nothing; add 'ordinary' to the finish line and one sentence naming the GTO as a thyristor whose gate can turn it off.
